fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with vertical reflective posts on both sides to define the access point during low-visibility or nighttime responses.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and equipment so responders can reach both structures without delay.
• Trim back dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back vegetation that may obscure sightlines along the access drive, particularly near any curves or the entrance.
• Post the address or a property map at the driveway entrance to help responders identify the locations of both detached structures relative to the main residence.
• Clear a path along the perimeter fencing to allow responders to move between the front and rear of the property on foot.
• If the perimeter fencing includes a rear gate, keep it unlocked or secure it with a standard Knox-type padlock for emergency access.
• If no rear gate exists, consider adding one to allow responders to reach the rear of the property without returning to the single access point.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structures to allow responders to approach and work around all sides of each building.
• Keep the open lawn area free of stored materials so it remains available as a staging area for equipment and personnel.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the house and any other structures on the property.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between the canopy and the building.
• Cut or mow the tall grass areas near the structure down to a short height.
• Keep grass cut short across the property, particularly between the structure and surrounding open terrain.
• Remove or cut back scattered shrubs that form a continuous line of vegetation running toward the structure.
• Separate low-hanging tree branches from nearby shrubs and tall grass to break the connection between ground-level vegetation and tree canopies.
• Clear dead grass, dry leaves, and loose plant debris from around the base of the structure.
• Move any woodpiles, stored materials, or other flammable items away from the exterior walls of the structure.
• Keep the single access driveway free of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and tall grass along both sides.
• Maintain the driveway surface and edges so vehicles, including emergency vehicles, can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the road during low-visibility conditions.
